title: Hong Kong national security police arrest man over allegedly importing ‘seditious’ books
zh_title: 香港国安警察逮捕涉嫌进口“煽动性”书籍的男子
summary: 香港国安警察在今年早些时候打击独立书店后的最新执法行动中逮捕了一名涉嫌进口“煽动性书籍”的男子。香港警队徽章。照片：Candice Chau/HKFP。警方周四在一份声明中表示，他们在旺角逮捕了一名 34 岁男子。他涉嫌“进口具有煽动意图的出版物”——触犯《维护国家安全条例》（又称《维护国家安全条例》第23条）。被捕者据悉是“等待鸟”项目经理布兰登·丘（Brandon Yau）
content:
香港国安警察在今年早些时候打击独立书店后的最新执法行动中逮捕了一名涉嫌进口“煽动性书籍”的男子。香港警队徽章。照片：Candice Chau/HKFP。警方周四在一份声明中表示，他们在旺角逮捕了一名 34 岁男子。他涉嫌“进口具有煽动意图的出版物”，这是《维护国家安全条例》（又称《维护国家安全条例》第23条）规定的犯罪行为。据了解，被捕者是“等待鸟”组织的项目经理布兰登·丘（Brandon Yau），该组织为因政治相关案件而入狱的人提供支持。这些书籍被进口并在其合作伙伴零售店 As One 销售，其收入归该集团所有。周一，Waiting Bird 在社交媒体上发帖称，海关从一批来自台湾的货物中查获了约 60 本书。该组织表示，没收的书籍是“对时事、个人经历和感受的理性讨论，与煽动意图没有任何关系”。警方在声明中表示，被捕者是一名公司董事，“涉嫌向当地书店进口煽动性书籍，意图向香港和中国政府带来仇恨、蔑视或不满”。作为爱德华王子中的一员。照片：Nidou Workspace，来自 Google 地图。
警方还搜查了该男子的住所和公司场所，查获了包括用于购买书籍的数字设备在内的物品，以及涉嫌具有煽动意图的文件和其他出版物。该男子已被拘留接受调查。进口具有煽动意图的出版物最高可判处七年监禁。香港当局今年加强了对独立书店的审查。书店老板表示，从台湾（许多中文书籍的来源地）订购的书籍经常受到海关检查。 Book Punch 的工作人员于 3 月份被捕，Hunter 书店的工作人员于 6 月份被捕。 7月，Have a Nice Stay和Greenfield书店的工作人员在同一天被捕。逮捕前一天，Have a Nice Stay 宣布将在运营四年后关闭。逮捕事件发生后，格林菲尔德书店还表示，明年租约到期后将关闭。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong national security police have arrested a man over allegedly importing “seditious books” in the latest law enforcement action following a crackdown on independent bookstores earlier this year. The Hong Kong Police Force emblem. Photo: Candice Chau/HKFP. Police said in a statement on Thursday that they had arrested a 34-year-old man in Mong Kok. He was suspected of “importing a publication that has a seditious intention” – a crime under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, also known as Article 23. The arrestee is understood to be Brandon Yau, a project manager at Waiting Bird, a group that supports people jailed in politics-related cases. The books were imported to be sold at As One, its partner retail outlet whose revenue goes towards the group. On Monday, Waiting Bird said in a social media post that Customs had seized around 60 books from a shipment that came from Taiwan. The group said the books confiscated were “rational discussions about current affairs, and personal experiences and feelings, with no connection whatsoever to seditious intentions.” In the statement, police said the person arrested was a company director “suspected of importing seditious books into local bookstores with the intent to bring hatred, contempt or disaffection” to the Hong Kong and Chinese governments. As One in Prince Edward. Photo: Nidou Workspace, via Google Maps. Officers also searched the man’s residence and company premises, seizing items including digital devices used to purchase the books, as well as documents and other publications suspected of having seditious intention. The man has been detained for investigation. Importing a publication with seditious intention carries a maximum sentence of seven years in jail. Hong Kong authorities have tightened scrutiny of independent bookstores this year. Bookstore owners have said that books ordered from Taiwan – the source for many Chinese-language titles – are frequently inspected by Customs. Staff from Book Punch were arrested in March, and staff from Hunter Bookstore were apprehended in June. In July, staff from Have a Nice Stay and Greenfield Bookstore were arrested on the same day. A day before the arrests, Have a Nice Stay announced it would close down after four years in operation. Following the arrests, Greenfield Bookstore also said it would shut after its lease expired next year.

title: Diamond Foundry Announces First-Ever D200mm Single-Crystal Diamond
zh_title: Diamond Foundry 宣布推出首款 D200mm 单晶金刚石
summary: Diamond Foundry Inc. 今天宣布了材料技术史上的一个重要里程碑：创造出第一颗 D200mm 单晶金刚石，直径为 200 毫米。这一成就标志着人类在半导体相关规模上制造金刚石作为技术材料的能力向前迈出了根本性的一步。在此公告中，Diamond Foundry 首席执行官 Martin Roscheisen 在中国宁波举行的 CarbonSemi 2026 展会上通过视频发表了主题演讲。观看主题演讲：https://youtu.be/ae0XQBDlLMQ 。钻石长期以来被认为是一种非凡的材料
content:
Diamond Foundry Inc. 今天宣布了材料技术史上的一个重要里程碑：创造出第一颗 D200mm 单晶金刚石，直径为 200 毫米。这一成就标志着人类在半导体相关规模上制造金刚石作为技术材料的能力向前迈出了根本性的一步。在此公告中，Diamond Foundry 首席执行官 Martin Roscheisen 在中国宁波举行的 CarbonSemi 2026 展会上通过视频发表了主题演讲。观看主题演讲：https://youtu.be/ae0XQBDlLMQ 。钻石长期以来被认为是一种非凡的技术材料。它将最高的导热率与卓越的机械强度、电绝缘性、光学特性以及极端电子性能的潜力结合在一起。然而，它在先进技术中的使用受到一个基本限制的限制：尺寸。 Diamond Foundry 的 D200mm 突破改变了这一点。生产 D200 毫米尺寸的单晶金刚石需要克服晶体生长、等离子体物理、反应堆工程、材料科学、过程控制和制造方面的基本挑战。结果不是单个金刚石片的组装，也不是多晶金刚石晶片。它是一颗直径为 200 毫米的单晶金刚石。 Diamond Foundry Inc. 首席执行官 Martin Roscheisen 表示：“这是曾经看似几乎不可能实现的里程碑之一。”数百名 DF 工程师、科学家和技术人员为我们实现这一目标做出了贡献。
它是十多年来无数实验、失败、发明、重建机器和见解的积累结果。” Roscheisen 特别认可 Stefan Gsell 和 Martin Fischer，他们在 25 年前就开始了单晶金刚石缩放工作。“Stefan 和 Martin 追求这个目标已经有 25 年了，”Roscheisen 说。 “在技术领域，很少有人能以这种毅力去应对真正艰巨的科学挑战。当普遍观点认为单晶钻石根本无法制造出如此规模时，他们继续前进。如今，这种毅力展现为首颗D200mm单晶钻石。最重要的是，它也使 D300mm 变得可预测。”从宝石尺寸到半导体尺寸 半导体行业是围绕晶圆级制造非凡材料的能力而建立的。硅向更大晶圆的发展改变了电子产品，允许经济且可重复地制造日益复杂的设备。钻石从未有过同等的缩放路径。天然钻石受到地质条件的限制。传统的实验室制造钻石历来被限制在相对较小的晶体尺寸。尽管金刚石的非凡特性与高功率电子、人工智能计算、光学、量子系统和其他先进技术越来越相关，但晶体尺寸仍然是一个基本瓶颈。
D200mm 单晶金刚石里程碑展示了一条超越这一限制的道路。对于 Diamond Foundry 来说，这一成就是更广泛努力的一部分，旨在将单晶金刚石从宝石中测量的稀有材料转变为大规模制造的科技工业半导体基材。当计算系统遇到越来越严格的热约束时，其影响尤为重要。现代人工智能处理器将大量能量集中到硅的微观区域。 Diamond 卓越的散热性能

【原文 English Original】
Diamond Foundry Inc. today announced a major milestone in the history of materials technology: the creation of the first-ever D200mm single-crystal diamond, measuring 200 millimeters in diameter. The achievement marks a fundamental step forward in humanity’s ability to manufacture diamond as a technology material at semiconductor-relevant scale. The announcement accompanies a keynote by Diamond Foundry CEO Martin Roscheisen, delivered by video at CarbonSemi 2026 in Ningbo, China. Watch the keynote: https://youtu.be/ae0XQBDlLMQ . Diamond has long been recognized as an extraordinary material for technology. It combines the highest thermal conductivity with exceptional mechanical strength, electrical insulation, optical properties, and the potential for extreme electronic performance. Yet its use in advanced technology has been constrained by one basic limitation: size. Diamond Foundry’s D200mm breakthrough changes that. Producing single-crystal diamond at D200mm scale required overcoming fundamental challenges in crystal growth, plasma physics, reactor engineering, materials science, process control, and manufacturing. The result is not an assembly of individual diamond pieces and not a polycrystalline diamond wafer. It is a single-crystal diamond at D200mm scale. “This is one of those milestones that once seemed almost impossible,” said Martin Roscheisen, CEO of Diamond Foundry Inc. “Hundreds of DF engineers, scientists, and technicians contributed to us getting here. It is the accumulated result of countless experiments, failures, inventions, rebuilt machines, and insights over more than a decade.” Roscheisen particularly recognized Stefan Gsell and Martin Fischer, whose work on scaling single-crystal diamond began 25 years ago. “Stefan and Martin pursued this goal for 25 years,” Roscheisen said. “There are very few examples in technology of someone sticking to a really hard scientific challenge with that level of perseverance. They kept going when the prevailing view was that single-crystal diamond simply could not be made at this scale. Today, the perseverance shows as the first-ever D200mm single-crystal diamond. And best of all, it makes D300mm predictable as well.” From Gemstone Dimensions to Semiconductor Dimensions The semiconductor industry is built around the ability to manufacture extraordinary materials at wafer scale. Silicon’s progression toward larger wafers transformed electronics by allowing increasingly sophisticated devices to be manufactured economically and repeatably. Diamond has never had an equivalent scaling path. Natural diamond is constrained by geology. Conventional lab-grown diamond has historically been constrained to relatively small crystal dimensions. Even as the extraordinary properties of diamond became increasingly relevant to high-power electronics, AI computing, optics, quantum systems, and other advanced technologies, crystal size remained a fundamental bottleneck. The D200mm single-crystal diamond milestone demonstrates a path beyond that limitation. For Diamond Foundry, the achievement is part of a broader effort to turn single-crystal diamond from a scarce material measured in gemstones into a tech-industrial semiconductor substrate manufactured at scale. The implications are particularly significant as computing systems encounter increasingly severe thermal constraints. Modern AI processors concentrate enormous amounts of power into microscopic regions of silicon. Diamond’s exceptional thermal conductivity can spread that heat at the material level, creating new possibilities for chip architectures, power densities, reliability, and cooling. Twenty-Five Years of Perseverance The D200mm achievement has roots extending well beyond Diamond Foundry itself. For 25 years, Gsell and Fischer pursued the underlying scientific and engineering challenge of growing high-quality single-crystal diamond of scalable size. Their work ultimately became part of a much larger effort involving hundreds of people across Diamond Foundry. The milestone reflects advances spanning plasma generation, growth chemistry, reactor architecture, crystal engineering, thermal management, metrology, automation, and manufacturing. “Technology history is often written around the moment something finally works,” Roscheisen said. “But that moment rests on the people who were willing to spend years — sometimes decades — making it work. This diamond exists because hundreds of people contributed, and because a few people refused to give up on the idea for 25 years.” A New Scale for Diamond Diamond Foundry views D200mm not as an endpoint, but as the beginning of a new manufacturing era for diamond. The company is developing single-crystal diamond for semiconductor and advanced-technology applications where diamond’s combination of thermal, mechanical, electrical, and optical properties can enable performance beyond the limits of conventional materials. The first D200mm crystal is shown as grown and unpolished — directly from the growth process. For a material that nature forms only under extraordinary conditions deep inside the Earth, the significance is simple: Single-crystal diamond has entered the wafer-scale era. content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

香港铁人三项世界杯混合接力获第11名 |中国劳工公告栏
2026 年 11 月 9 日星期一 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻（英文）
香港铁人三项世界杯混合接力赛获第11名
香港队于2026年11月8日举行的铁人三项世界杯香港赛段的混合接力赛中获得第11名。由罗景斌、韦奇、蔡恩彦和叶德朗组成的队伍以1小时31分39秒的成绩完赛。瑞士获得金牌，俄罗斯获得银牌，中国获得铜牌。
2026 年 11 月 8 日 19:09 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 9 日 04:25 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
铁人三项世界杯香港赛段于11月8日在中环及湾仔海滨举行混合接力赛。比赛于11月7日开始，历时两天。
混合接力赛中，每队由两名男子和两名女子组成。每个运动员都完成了 300 米游泳、7.4 公里自行车和 2 公里跑步，然后才标记下一位队友。最后一名选手冲过龙和路的终点线。
瑞士队以1小时28分51秒的成绩获得第一名。俄罗斯队获得第二名，中国队获得第三名。
香港派出的代表队包括在名古屋亚运会混合接力赛中获得铜牌的卢景斌和魏琪，以及蔡恩彦和叶德朗。他们以1小时31分39秒的成绩完成比赛，获得总成绩第11名。

Hong Kong finishes 11th in triathlon World Cup mixed relay | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 9 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong finishes 11th in triathlon World Cup mixed relay
Hong Kong placed 11th in the mixed relay at the Triathlon World Cup Hong Kong leg on 8 November 2026. The team of Lo King-pan, Wei Qi, Choi Yan-yin and Yip Tak-long finished in 1 hour 31 minutes 39 seconds. Switzerland won gold, Russia silver and China bronze.
8 Nov 2026 at 19:09 HKT · updated 9 Nov, 04:25 · 1 min read
The Triathlon World Cup Hong Kong leg concluded on 8 November with the mixed relay event held along the Central and Wan Chai waterfront. The competition began on 7 November and ran over two days.
In the mixed relay, each team consisted of two men and two women. Every athlete completed a 300-metre swim, a 7.4-kilometre cycle and a two-kilometre run before tagging the next teammate. The final runner crossed the finish line on Lung Wo Road.
Switzerland claimed first place with a time of 1 hour 28 minutes 51 seconds. Russia finished second, and China took third.
Hong Kong fielded a team including Lo King-pan and Wei Qi, who won bronze in the mixed relay at the Asian Games in Nagoya, together with Choi Yan-yin and Yip Tak-long. They completed the race in 1 hour 31 minutes 39 seconds, finishing 11th overall.

content: 文章来源：rfa 记者：Alan Lu 流亡海外的中国媒体人程万军指控，台湾移民署在遣返他回泰国、押送他登机期间，曾对他捆绑、堵嘴及殴打。 (图截取自程万军视频) 曾任中国央视《法律讲堂》主讲人的程万军，周二(3日)在台湾桃园机场寻求人道庇护，随后被遣返泰国。他11月4日公开指控，台湾移民署人员押送他登机期间，曾对他捆绑、堵嘴及殴打。 程万军搭乘的班机原定从泰国曼谷经台湾转机返回北京，他11月2日抵达桃园机场后，向移民署人员表示自己遭受中共政治迫害，希望暂时留在台湾，等待前往第三国寻求庇护。 不过，台湾主管机关审查后未同意其申请，并于3日晚间将他送返曼谷。 程万军4日向自由亚洲电台指控移民署人员在执行遣返过程中，将他捆绑押送，并以毛巾堵嘴、口罩蒙面及勒住手腕等方式限制行动。他还指控自己在机上遭到殴打，身体多处受伤，抵达曼谷后前往医疗机构接受急救。 程万军称，有移民署人员曾对他说“你的死活与我们无关”，并批评台湾陆委会没有详细审查其提交的材料，便决定将他遣返。他表示，将向台湾监察院及法院提出控告。 上述程万军有关遭捆绑、殴打及台湾官员言论的说法，本台无法独立核实。 台湾移民署回应表示，程万军未能就其诉求提出具体事证，不符合援助条件及资格，且没有有效入境许可，因此依《入出国及移民法》第50条，将他送返泰国曼谷。 移民署同时表示，程万军在登机过程中极力抗拒，并出现“自伤”行为，因此采取必要措施维护飞航安全，相关作为均属依法行政。移民署的声明未逐项回应程万军所称遭到殴打，以及有官员发表不当言论等指控。 程万军提供照片，称自己遭受殴打，以致身体多处受伤，并于抵达曼谷后前往医疗机构接受急救。  (程万军提供) 陆委会：无法核实遭迫害情形 台湾陆委会4日发布声明表示，每年都会发生多起中国人士在台湾机场寻求暂时留置的类似案件，政府必须建立甄别机制，不可能每件申请都予以接受。 陆委会指出，本案的主要关键，是政府无法核实程万军所称遭受迫害的情况。除当事人本人的声明外，目前没有其他第三方事证可以佐证；程万军也能够自由进出中国，没有受到人身自由限制。因此，主管机关只能依既有机制将他送回泰国。 陆委会强调，台湾政府对中国异议人士一向抱持尽量援助的立场，但有关申请仍须遵守台湾法律及国境管理制度。 程万军则表示，他离开中国后曾在泰国发表反对中共的言论，因此担心遭遣返回中国。目前他的泰国签证即将到期，正透过独立中文笔会及加拿大救援团队，申请前往第三国避难。 台湾学者：应评估未来风险 台湾华人民主书院协会理事长曾建元接受本台采访时表示，庇护审查不应只判断当事人过去是否已经遭受政治迫害，也应评估其未来遭迫害的风险。 他说，程万军能够合法离开中国，并不代表返国后没有风险。程万军在抵达泰国后发表的反共言论，可能增加他被遣返后遭到追究的危险。审查重点应是这种风险是否存在及程度高低，而不是等到迫害事实已经发生，才考虑是否提供保护。 曾建元指出，台湾至今没有通过《难民法》，政治庇护也缺乏完整的法律及行政程序。政府只能针对个案作出政治判断及职权裁量，容易受到不同时空、两岸关系及国际环境影响，也可能产生处理标准前后不一的问题。 他建议，即使《难民法》短期内难以通过，台湾政府至少应制定行政命令，明确申请条件、审查程序、所需证据及驳回理由，并让民间团体及申请人了解决定依据。 “每个个案都是政治决定，这并不好。”曾建元说，建立公开标准，才能使申请人知道可能面对哪些风险，也能让政府的处理立场较为一致。 近年已有多名中国维权人士在桃园机场转机时寻求庇护。2023年，陈思明在没有入境台湾的情况下，最终获准前往加拿大；今年9月，为北京锡安教会辩护的律师王夏红一家，也获台湾暂时人道安置。但其他数起申请者则遭送返前一出发地。 曾建元认为，台湾社会对于接纳难民仍缺乏高度共识，朝野政党也多半回避相关立法，因此《难民法》何时能够通过仍不乐观。程万军案再次凸显，在缺乏明确法律及审查标准的情况下，台湾如何处理中国异议人士的庇护申请，仍高度依赖政府对个案作出的行政裁量。

title: Bank of England pours cold water on AI productivity boom
zh_title: 英格兰银行给人工智能生产力繁荣泼冷水
summary: 英国央行表示，尽管在人工智能领域投入了数十亿美元，但该技术并没有为英国企业带来生产力的提高。在最新的货币政策报告中，央行发现过去三年人工智能使英国生产力提高了约 0.5%。这意味着自 2024 年初以来，年生产率仅额外增长 0.1 至 0.2 个百分点，这远不是硅谷所希望的经济革命。 “人工智能投资似乎对当前的需求强度有所贡献，但
content:
英国央行表示，尽管在人工智能领域投入了数十亿美元，但该技术并没有为英国企业带来生产力的提高。在最新的货币政策报告中，央行发现过去三年人工智能使英国生产力提高了约 0.5%。这意味着自 2024 年初以来，年生产率仅额外增长 0.1 至 0.2 个百分点，这远不是硅谷所希望的经济革命。英国央行表示：“人工智能投资似乎对当前的需求强劲做出了一定贡献，但到目前为止，只有证据表明人工智能推动了英国生产率增长的适度增长。”即使是被认为最有可能从这项技术中受益的行业也没有什么值得夸耀的。信息和通信等人工智能密集型行业的生产率增长有所改善，但尚未超过大流行前的平均水平。这并不是说人工智能没有为英国经济做任何事情。该银行估计，自 2026 年初以来，人工智能相关活动占英国 GDP 增长的近五分之一，尽管其中大部分似乎来自开发和部署该技术的公司，而不是通过使用该技术提高生产力的企业。
报告称：“迄今为止，人工智能对经济增长的贡献似乎反映了人工智能技术上游开发和实施的活动，而不是在经济其他领域采用人工智能技术所带来的更广泛的收益。”换句话说，事实证明，销售人工智能比实际使用它更有利可图。该银行还警告称，不要将英国近期生产率提高的功劳过多地归功于人工智能。增长的主要原因似乎是企业雇用的工人减少了，而产出却持续增长，部分原因是企业放松了大流行后的人员配置决定并应对更高的就业成本。尽管预测人工智能将导致大量劳动力失业，但接受世行决策者小组调查的公司报告称，迄今为止对就业几乎没有总体影响。然而，这项技术使得一些雇主不太愿意雇用新员工或替换离职员工。其他研究表明，企业仍在等待回报。 Gartner 上个月发布的一项调查发现，虽然四分之三的企业董事会成员期望人工智能能够提高生产力并削减成本，但只有 3% 的组织实际上实现了目标。与此同时，38% 的人在人工智能方面的支出已经超出预算，但 85% 的人计划明年支出更多。
2 月份发布的另一项涉及近 6,000 名高管的研究发现，超过 80% 的公司没有看到人工智能对就业或生产力产生明显影响。显然，解决令人失望的回报的答案是继续写支票。人工智能支出与实际回报之间日益脱节也引起了金融监管机构的注意。国际货币基金组织上个月警告称，如果承诺的利润没有兑现，人工智能支出热潮可能会再次给投资者带来损失，并可能拖累更广泛的经济。国际清算银行 (Bank for International Settlements) 在 6 月份发出了类似的警报，将当前的支出热潮与 20 世纪 90 年代的互联网泡沫进行了比较。它担心的是，科技巨头正在向基础设施投入巨额资金，因为他们假设人工智能最终将带来同样巨大的回报，例如

【原文 English Original】
Despite the billions being thrown at artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered little in the way of productivity gains for UK businesses, according to the Bank of England. In its latest Monetary Policy Report , the central bank found that AI has increased UK productivity by an estimated 0.5 percent over the past three years. That works out to just 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points of additional annual productivity growth since early 2024, hardly the economic revolution Silicon Valley has been promising. "AI investment appears to be contributing somewhat to current demand strength, but so far there is only evidence of a modest AI-driven rise in UK productivity growth," the Bank said. Even industries supposedly best placed to benefit from the technology have little to boast about. Productivity growth has improved in AI-heavy sectors such as information and communications, but has yet to exceed pre-pandemic averages. That's not to say AI isn't doing anything for the British economy. The bank estimates that AI-related activity has accounted for just under a fifth of UK GDP growth since the beginning of 2026, though much of that appears to come from companies developing and deploying the technology rather than businesses becoming more productive by using it. "The contribution to growth from AI to date appears to reflect activity in the upstream development and implementation of AI technologies rather than broader gains from their adoption elsewhere in the economy," the report said. In other words, selling AI is proving rather more lucrative than actually using it, The bank also cautioned against giving AI too much credit for Britain's recent productivity improvements. Much of the increase appears to reflect businesses hiring fewer workers while output continues to grow, partly as companies unwind post-pandemic staffing decisions and respond to higher employment costs. And despite predictions that AI will make vast swathes of the workforce redundant, firms responding to the Bank's Decision Maker Panel survey reported virtually no overall impact on employment so far. The technology is, however, making some employers less inclined to hire new staff or replace those who leave. Other studies suggest businesses are still waiting for the payoff. A Gartner survey published last month found that while three-quarters of corporate board members expected AI to improve productivity and cut costs, just 3 percent of organizations had actually achieved their targets. Meanwhile, 38 percent were already over budget on AI spending, yet 85 percent planned to spend even more next year. Another study involving nearly 6,000 executives , published in February, found that more than 80 percent of firms had seen no discernible impact from AI on either employment or productivity. Apparently, the answer to disappointing returns is to keep writing checks. That growing disconnect between AI spending and actual returns has also caught the attention of financial watchdogs. The International Monetary Fund warned last month that the AI spending spree could come back to bite investors if the promised profits don't show up, potentially dragging the wider economy down with it. The Bank for International Settlements sounded a similar alarm in June , comparing the current spending spree to the dotcom boom of the 1990s. Its concern is that tech giants are committing enormous sums to infrastructure on the assumption that AI will eventually deliver equally enormous returns, leaving them exposed if reality fails to cooperate. However, AI is already making its presence felt in one area: prices. The Bank of England noted that surging demand for AI-related products, including memory chips, has pushed up export prices in China and other Asian economies, raising import costs for Britain. So while businesses are still waiting for their AI-powered productivity windfall, the costs of the boom are already making their way through the economy. The bank isn't writing off the technology just yet. Businesses surveyed expect AI to add around 0.9 percentage points to annual productivity growth over the next three years, with the gains split roughly equally between faster output growth and slower employment growth. It seems the AI industry's most impressive productivity achievement is convincing businesses to keep opening their wallets. ®

安斯泰来员工将于 12 月从中国监狱释放
一名日本安斯泰来制药员工因在中国从事间谍活动被判处三年半徒刑，预计将于 12 月 14 日获释并返回日本。 |路透社

北京——消息人士周六称，安斯泰来制药公司的一名日本员工因在中国从事间谍活动被判处三年零六个月徒刑，预计将于 12 月中旬获释并返回日本。
据消息人士透露，最终安排将于12月14日释放这家日本制药公司的60多岁员工。
2023年3月，该员工在结束北京工作后准备离开中国时突然被中国当局拘留。他于 2024 年 8 月被起诉。

Astellas employee to be released from China prison in December
A Japanese Astellas Pharma employee sentenced to three and a half years in prison for espionage in China is expected to be released on Dec. 14 and return to Japan. | REUTERS
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Beijing – A Japanese employee of Astellas Pharma, who was sentenced to three years and six months in prison for espionage in China, is expected to be released in mid-December and return to Japan, sources said Saturday.
According to sources, final arrangements are being made to release the employee of the Japanese pharmaceutical company in his 60s on Dec. 14.
The employee was suddenly detained by Chinese authorities in March 2023, when he was about to leave China after the end of his Beijing assignment. He was indicted in August 2024.

content:
11月7日在上海举行的第九届中国国际进口博览会上，香港丝袜奶茶吸引观众。 （中新社）
（北京综合讯）随着肥胖与糖尿病风险上升，中国专家及官媒提议借当下消费税改革契机，对含糖饮料进行分级征税，促使民众减少糖分摄入。
据香港《南华早报》报道，中共中央机关报《人民日报》及相关平台近几个月均刊文讨论糖税。例如，人民日报社主办的《健康时报》7月刊发的一篇报道称，中国超重和肥胖者的比例已超50%，精制糖摄入过量是重要诱因。
文章指出，征收含糖税或许是大势所趋，并建议中国从审慎研究并有序试点开始，按含糖量设置阶梯税率，高糖高税、低糖轻税、无糖免税，并将税收定向用于校园健康饮食项目等。
在中国多数便利店里，含糖饮料依然是最容易获得、价格较低的商品之一。
截至2024年7月，全球至少有116个国家对至少一种含糖饮料征收国家级消费税。世界卫生组织去年7月呼吁各国对含糖饮料征收至少达到零售价20%的税率，目标是到2035年将含糖饮料整体价格提高50%。
明年3月，中国新版预包装食品营养标签规定将生效，届时预包装食品的营养标签将须强制标示糖和饱和脂肪含量。
这一举措引发外界对中国可能开征糖税的预期。与此同时，中国正推进消费税改革，拟调整征税范围、税率和征收环节，也为开征糖税提供契机。
北京大学公共卫生学院教授傅虹桥去年在《柳叶刀》发表的一篇论文称，若将含糖饮料、烟草和酒类价格提高20%，到2050年可挽救135万人的生命。
对外经济贸易大学教授郑榕则预计，若对含糖饮料征税使售价增加二至三成，每年可为国家增收1700亿至2360亿元人民币（326亿至452亿新元），可用作公共卫生资金。
但专家也提醒，现制奶茶等现调饮料可能成为糖税征管漏洞，促使消费者转向未征税的品类，导致糖税失去约束力。
人民日报健康客户端引述多名专家指出，含糖饮料税迟迟未能落地，并非简单的没有意识到问题。“在某些阶段，健康问题还不足以压倒其他政策目标。”

它成立于 2023 年，据报道由黄乐有限公司所有，由黄乐女士或 Alice Huang 领导，同年被出售给 Swiftdata。次年，Megaspeed 通过 Speedmatrix 注册成立，该子公司在马来西亚柔佛州设有两个办事处。该子公司是走私指控的中心。对黄乐或爱丽丝黄的研究揭示了不一致的地方。有报道称，她的职业生涯始于湖南卫视和中央电视台的一名电视记者，但前者的一位高管声称从未听说过她，而后者则没有她的个人资料。在从事媒体工作后，她进入银行和金融领域，担任汇丰银行私人银行部门总裁助理，然后成为中国金融服务公司中信证券的副总裁。目前还不清楚她之后是如何加入 Megaspeed 的，但黄女士似乎在上海和浙江周围建立了一个由公司和投资者组成的网络，积极推动手机游戏公司转向人工智能数据中心。人们质疑像 Megaspeed 这样的小公司为何会无缘无故地投入如此大的精力购买 Nvidia AI GPU，但这确实引起了黄仁勋的注意。在该公司下了大笔订单后，人们发现爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 在 LinkedIn 帖子中与黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 以及技嘉 (Gigabyte) 和 NetThunder 的其他行业高管一起喝酒。

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia chief Jensen Huang is the center of a new controversy as the U.S. intelligence community believes that he had a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. According to the Financial Times , Alice Huang, sometimes referred to as Huang Le, was a top executive at Singaporean firm Megaspeed and was reportedly romantically involved with the CEO of the world's largest AI chip manufacturer. Notably, Jensen is currently married to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang. It’s unclear whether Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS) before she joined Megaspeed or after she had already established a business relationship with Jensen, but it’s been reported that the suspected agent was apparently targeting the Nvidia head to help Chinese companies gain access to banned AI chips. Go deeper with TH Premium: AI shortages (Image credit: Nvidia) AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supply Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible Chip scarcity assaults auto industry amid the worsening Nexperia and DRAM crisis The custom AI ASIC state of play Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via its subsidiary Speedmatrix, although Nvidia insists the company has no ties to China. Megaspeed sits at the center of a web of companies linked to China, and it was previously connected to a Chinese gaming company called 7Road International. It was founded in 2023 and reportedly owned by Huang Le Limited, led by Ms. Huang Le, or Alice Huang, before it was sold to Swiftdata that same year. The following year, Megaspeed used Speedmatrix to incorporate, with the subsidiary having two offices in Johor, Malaysia. The subsidiary is at the center of the smuggling allegations. Research into Huang Le, or Alice Huang, has revealed inconsistencies. There were reports that she started her career as a TV journalist working for Hunan TV and Chinese state broadcaster China Central Television (CCTV), but an executive at the former claims to have never heard of her, while she does not have a profile under the latter. After her supposed stint in media, she moved into banking and finance as assistant to the president of HSBC’s private banking division before becoming vice president at CITIC Securities, a Chinese financial services company. It’s unclear how she became involved with Megaspeed after that, but it seems Ms. Huang built a network of companies and investors around Shanghai and Zhejiang that aggressively pushed mobile gaming companies toward AI data centers. Questions arose about how a small company like Megaspeed could commit so much to buying Nvidia AI GPUs seemingly out of nowhere, but it certainly caught Jensen Huang's attention. After the company made its massive order, Alice Huang was spotted in a LinkedIn post hanging out for drinks with Jensen Huang and other industry executives from Gigabyte and NetThunder. She was once again seen standing behind the Nvidia chief, alongside other people, one year later as he exited a Taiwan restaurant. Nvidia has denied the allegations, saying Jensen Huang meets with thousands of customer executives annually and that they exchange ordinary business information — not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets or national security information. China has also said that these accusations of espionage on Jensen Huang by the MSS are just “groundless smears and slanders” against Beijing. However, foreign intelligence agencies also routinely conduct “honeypot” operations, using operatives to ensnare targets into relationships to extract data and gain insight into industry secrets. While these operations traditionally targeted politicians, members of the military, and their staff, the Lansing Institute suggests that “China is employing ‘attractive women’ posing as investors, business professionals, academics, or romantic partners to gain access to U.S. tech talent, networks, and research infrastructure.”
